newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPALS -- firm but dreading refundings.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPALS -- firm but dreading refundings.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds were flat to up an 1/8 in early trade on Wednesday, but the prospect that more refundings will sweep into the market prevented prices from rising as much as Treasuries.
"We're seeing a lot of refunding deals come into the market...They're going to keep coming and that's going to limit our upside," a trader said.
Issuers increasingly are refinancing existing bonds because the recent interest rate drop in the fixed-income markets has made such deals economic.

As a result, the municipal market recently has lagged the Treasury market, a scenario seen likely to continue for a bit longer. Further, demand for municipal bonds has slackened as yields have fallen.
"It's tough to get our customers' attention," the trader said.
The City and County of Denver, Colorado, had a balance of $22.4 million out of a total offering of $39.955 million of Certificates of Participation.

Maryland's competitive sale of $250 million of general obligations, however, was expected to go fairly smoothly as the state's triple-A paper is considered attractive. The competitive offering was scheduled for 1100 EDT.
Buying interest in secondary issues has waned, as demand centers on new issues with more attractive structures.
In contrast to the rising supply of new issues, the main yardstick for the secondary market slackened. The Standard and Poor's Corp Blue List slipped to $1.290 billion from $1.309 billion.

The roster of economic reports due out on Wednesday included new home sales for June, which were predicted at 818,000 units, down from 825,000 in the previous month, according to a Reuters survey of economists. The report was due out at 1000 EDT.

The market also looked ahead to the Treasury's quarterly refunding announcement, slated for 1300 EDT. Analysts forecast that the Treasury would sell $16 billion of three-year notes, down from $17 billion in the last issue. Ten-year notes were predicted at $14 billion, up from $12 billion, while the 30-year issue was seen at $10 billion, unchanged.
In the secondary market, Fairfax County, Virginia, Water Authority Water Revenues of 2029, which pay a five percent coupon, were bid at 5.28 percent, NET, down two basis points.
And Harris County, Texas, Refunding Toll Road bonds of 2024, which carry a five percent coupon, were bid at 5.25 percent, NET, down three basis points.

In Chicago futures markets, September municipal bond futures gained six ticks to 121-24/32, slightly outpaced by September Treasury bond futures, which climbed eight ticks to 116-6/32. This left the MOB spread at plus 176 ticks, down from the close at 180 ticks.
Municipal bond sales for Wednesday were expected to total $1.2 billion in 32 sales, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Negotiated offerings totalled $858 million in 18 sales, with a $340 million California Natural Resources offering through PaineWebber Inc topping the list.
On the competitive side, 14 sales totaling $370 million were scheduled.
